subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — IP / Training redlines
messages:
From: Asha Verma <asha.verma@opalhealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: d.chen@opalhealth.com, procure@opalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: redlines on IP / training

Marissa —

Thanks for sending the latest MSA and order form. Our legal team reviewed and attached a tracked redline focusing on IP and downstream use (see OpalHealth_MSA_OrderForm_Redline_asha.docx). High-level concerns:

- Output ownership: Opal wants explicit assignment of productized outputs that derive from our customer content (we flagged assignment language in §7).
- Training/retrain: Opal is asking for a carveout that would allow model retraining on customer prompts/content unless we explicitly opt-out; they want a stronger affirmative consent model.
- Feedback license: they propose a broad perpetual license for feedback and telemetry to be used for improvements without attribution or restrictions.

From Opal's perspective these items are deal breakers for product teams, so they want clear language and evidence that customer data won't be used to train general models without consent. They also asked for evidence of telemetry isolation and a SOC-2 style description of logs/audit.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on: (1) assignment vs. license for downstream outputs, (2) whether Opal content can be used in any model training absent express opt-in, and (3) whether a scoped feedback license limited to non-attributable telemetry for service improvements is acceptable?

We are aiming to finalize the MSA/order form by next week. Please let me know if you'd like to set a short call with our procurement counsel.

Thanks,
Asha Verma
Senior Counsel — Contracts
OpalHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: redlines on IP / training

Asha —

Appreciate the detailed pass and the tracked file. Short answers up front so your team has clarity while we pull legal language:

1) Output ownership: Redwood's standard is to grant customers rights to use outputs produced for them; we do not assign model IP. We can accept language that guarantees unrestricted use of the generated output for Opal's productization, subject to the usual limitations (no transfer of Redwood model weights).

2) Training/retrain: Redwood does NOT train general-purpose models on customer PII/content without explicit opt-in. We can agree to an opt-in model for retraining and propose explicit opt-in checkboxes in the order form.

3) Feedback license: we are open to a scoped feedback/telemetry license for service improvements, limited to aggregated/non-attributable signals and excluding customer content used for model training unless explicitly opted-in.

Ben and Laura — looping you in to confirm wording and to propose concrete edits to their tracked document. We will prepare a counter-tracked with our compromise language and a short summary matrix (attached) that maps each Opal ask to Redwood position and rationale.

Asha — would you be available for a 30-min call on Monday 6/7 to walk counsel through the proposed compromises? If so we can send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OpalHealth redlines — internal suggested responses

Team — forwarding Opal's redline. Suggested negotiation positions below; Laura, can you draft counters?

Summary of Opal asks (from Asha):
- Assignment of outputs to Opal (they want broader assignment than our typical license)
- Implied right to retrain unless we opt-out (they asked for a default affirmative right)
- Broad feedback license for improvements (no attribution/limitations)

Redwood suggested responses (draft talking points):
1) Output ownership: we concede full use rights for generated outputs and grant Opal a perpetual, worldwide, transferable license to outputs produced from their content. We push back on assignment of our underlying model or weights. (Reason: product teams get commercial comfort without Redwood transferring core IP).

2) Training/retrain: propose "opt-in" language. Default = no training on customer content. Offer an ordered path: (a) telemetry + aggregated signals allowed for service quality improvements, (b) explicit, auditable opt-in checkbox per order form for using customer content in model retraining, (c) provide Opal a documented export/notification workflow if they opt-in.

3) Feedback license: agree to a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback/telemetry for service improvements and bug fixes, limited to aggregated telemetry and stripped of customer content. Exclude PII and training unless opt-in.

Ask list for Laura:
- Prepare counter-tracked changes with concrete clause language for §§7, 9, and the order form opt-in exhibit.
- Add a short "Evidence & Controls" paragraph citing our telemetry separation, retention, and audit logs (SOC-like summary) to attach to the counter.
- Confirm whether the opt-in checkbox language can be surfaced in order form UI and propose operational steps for customer-requested model removal.

Ben — fine for me to propose a 30-min legal sync Monday 6/7 at 10:00 PT with Opal? If not I can offer alternative times.

Thanks,
Marissa

Asha —

Thanks for the redline and for surfacing Opal's priorities. Attached is a counter-tracked that incorporates the positions we discussed:

- Output: Redwood grants Opal a perpetual, worldwide, transferrable license to Outputs (defined as content generated by the Service using Opal data). We make explicit that Redwood's model weights and internal training artifacts are not assigned.
- Training: Default = no training on customer content. We add an "Order Form Opt-In for Model Retraining" exhibit with clear checkboxes and audit logging. If Opal opts in, we will provide an addendum outlining retention, deletion, and a one-quarter notice before incorporating customer data into general model training.
- Feedback: We accept a scoped, non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback license limited to aggregated telemetry and service improvements, expressly excluding customer content unless Opal opts in via the exhibit.

I've attached the tracked file: Redwood_Opal_Response_TRACKED.docx. Laura included a short "Evidence & Controls" appendix that summarizes our telemetry isolation, retention windows, and audit log process.

Would you be available Monday 6/7 at 10:00 AM PT for a 30-min call with procurement/legal to walk through the counter? If that doesn't work, propose two times and we will accommodate.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
